edges.description: Loss of NECAP1 places a synaptic-vesicle trafficking defect upstream of the shared network dysfunction of this anchor. The authors frame the link as newly connecting this trafficking pathway to early infantile epileptic encephalopathy, and the intermediate steps between reduced clathrin-mediated synaptic endocytosis and network hyperexcitability are not established.

edges.description: Abnormal developing brain network function contributes to early seizures.
Genetic etiologies and epileptic activity contribute to impaired development.

Epileptiform and suppression-burst EEG patterns are the electrographic expression of the hyperexcitable developing network this node describes, which is why they are used to define these presentations.

The developmental arm of the encephalopathy presents clinically as global developmental delay, which in an early-childhood epilepsy cohort affected 49% of children twenty-four months after presentation.
The cognitive arm of the same developmental impairment presents as intellectual disability once the child is old enough to be assessed.
In the severe presentations the developmental arm is not only delay but loss of already-acquired motor, cognitive and behavioural skills after seizure onset.

A substantial fraction of these early-onset seizure disorders fail to come under control on antiseizure medication: 36% of children in an early-childhood epilepsy cohort had drug-resistant epilepsy twenty-four months after presentation.

nodes.description: NECAP1 encodes a clathrin-accessory protein that acts on the AP-2 adaptor in clathrin-mediated endocytosis at synapses. The founding family's homozygous truncating allele triggers nonsense-mediated decay, which is consistent with loss of the gene product rather than a dominant-negative mechanism, and the same study reports NECAP1 as highly enriched in the central nervous system. This is the only gene-specific mechanism modelled as its own node in this entry. Three child classes of the anchor lack a dedicated dismech entry - DEE21, DEE33 and DEE45 - but only NECAP1 has a mechanism worked out at this level of detail; EEF1A2 and GABRB1 are bound as etiologies on the shared convergence node instead.
